title: Marx on Work and Class
objective: After this level you can explain why Karl Marx thought workers under capitalism were alienated, and the main objections critics raised.
summary: Marx held that capitalist work alienates workers from product, work, others and their nature; critics question his view of human nature, and Nozick his theory of exploitation.

cards.headline: Why does work so often feel like it belongs to someone else?
cards.body: Karl Marx gave that feeling a name, alienation, and blamed it on the way capitalism organizes work.

cards.headline: Four separations
cards.body: In his Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, unpublished when he died, Marx named four ways workers under capitalism are alienated. They are cut off from the product, which they neither own nor control and which comes to dominate them; from the work itself, which drains them; from other people; and from their own human nature.

mascot.line: Keep the four in order: the product, the work, other people, yourself. Each is something the worker is cut off from.

cards.headline: Work could be different
cards.body: Why call this a loss rather than just life? Because Marx held that work can be creative and fulfilling, a central part of what it is to be human. He rejected the view of work as a necessary evil. If work can be where we flourish, then work that only earns a living has taken something from us.

cards.headline: Critics reply
cards.body: Critics push back on two fronts. First, the diagnosis rests on a claim about human nature: someone who thought people are by nature solitary and selfish could agree that work breeds isolation, yet deny it’s alienation. Second, Marx also charged capitalism with exploitation, resting on the labour theory of value (a good’s value is set by the labour in it). Robert Nozick (1974) replied that if that theory fails, the exploitation charge collapses too.

cards.headline: Marx on Work and Class: the big picture
learned: Alienated from product, work, others, and self
Work could be creative and fulfilling
Critics: it depends on a view of human nature
Nozick: exploitation needs the labour theory of value

questions.prompt: According to Marx’s 1844 Manuscripts, workers under capitalism are alienated from _____.

options.label: their national government
options.rationale: It isn’t one of his four.

options.label: the weather and the seasons
options.rationale: It isn’t one of his four.

options.label: their town’s local laws
options.rationale: It isn’t one of his four.

questions.explanation: Marx’s four: the product, the work, other people and the worker’s own human nature.

questions.prompt: Why did Marx see alienated work as a real loss, not just a fact of life?

options.label: He held work could be creative and central to being human
He thought all human work should one day be abolished
options.rationale: He wanted work transformed, not abolished.

options.label: He believed only machines should ever do any real work
options.rationale: His picture is of fulfilling human work.

options.label: He thought wages were fixed by nature and could not change
options.rationale: His complaint is about how work is organized.

questions.explanation: Marx held that work can be creative and fulfilling, so work that frustrates this takes something from us.

questions.prompt: Put these works on society and education in order of when they were written, from earliest to latest.
items: Vindication of the Rights of Woman
questions.explanation: Rousseau’s Emile came out in 1762 and Wollstonecraft’s Vindication in 1792. Marx wrote his Manuscripts in 1844 (unpublished when he died), and Mill’s On Liberty appeared in 1859.
